title: Secure Headers, Rate Limits & Timeouts
objectives: Apply security headers and name the attack each stops
Limit body size and request rates per route

examples.name: limits.js
examples.code:
import helmet from "helmet"
import rateLimit from "express-rate-limit"

app.use(helmet())                          // CSP, HSTS, nosniff, frameguard
app.use(express.json({ limit: "1mb" }))    // memory exhaustion defense
app.use("/api/auth", rateLimit({ windowMs: 60_000, limit: 10 }))  // brute force

const server = app.setTimeout(30_000)      // slow-loris / hung clients

exercise.prompt: Match defense to attack: "helmet frameguard" (clickjacking), "1mb body limit" (memory exhaustion), "rate limit /auth" (credential stuffing), "HSTS" (protocol downgrade).
hints: Every hardening line should name the attack it stops.
Unlimited bodies + rate-less auth are the two classic holes.

options: XSS amplification, sniffing, clickjacking, downgrade attacks
questions.explanation: Headers do not fix injection; they cap browser-side attack classes.

questions.prompt: Without request timeouts, a slow client can…
questions.explanation: Hung sockets pin memory and connections — timeouts reclaim them.
